_meta.indication: First-line treatment of patients with metastatic NSCLC whose tumors have EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 (L858R) substitution mutations as detected by an FDA-approved test

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (2:1), open-label, active-controlled, multicenter, multinational trial comparing afatinib monotherapy to pemetrexed/cisplatin chemotherapy as first-line treatment
pivotal_trials.population: First-line, EGFR TKI-naïve patients with EGFR mutation-positive, metastatic (Stage IV and Stage IIIb with pleural/pericardial effusion) non-small cell lung cancer (adenocarcinoma)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Progression-free survival (PFS) assessed by central independent review per RECIST v1.1
pivotal_trials.n: 345 patients randomized (2:1): GILOTRIF N=230, Pemetrexed/Cisplatin N=115
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant PFS improvement: median PFS 11.1 vs 6.9 months; HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.43, 0.78), p<0.001. No statistically significant OS difference (median OS 28.1 vs 28.2 months).

nct_ctgov.title: BIBW 2992 (Afatinib) Versus Chemotherapy as First Line Treatment in NSCLC With EGFR Mutation

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%): diarrhea (96%, Grade 3 15%), rash/dermatitis acneiform (90%, Grade 3 16%), stomatitis (71%), paronychia (58%), dry skin (31%), pruritus (21%), decreased appetite. Serious adverse reactions in 29% of patients; most frequent diarrhea (6.6%) and vomiting (4.8%).
target_moa: Kinase inhibitor: afatinib covalently binds the kinase domains of EGFR (ErbB1), HER2 (ErbB2) and HER4 (ErbB4) and irreversibly inhibits tyrosine kinase autophosphorylation, downregulating ErbB signaling
companion_dx_detail: therascreen EGFR RGQ PCR Kit detecting EGFR exon 19 deletions and exon 21 (L858R) substitution mutations, approved concurrent with afatinib

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the NDA was not referred to the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee because outside expertise was not necessary and there were no controversial issues

description.text: Expanded indication to include metastatic NSCLC with non-resistant EGFR mutations beyond exon 19 deletions or exon 21 (L858R)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides updates to expand the approved indication to include treatment of patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose tumors have non-resistant epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations as detected by an FDA-approved test, which includes additional mutations other than EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 (L858R) substitution mutations. In addition, the Limitation of Use was modified for the approved indication to denote that safety and efficacy have not been established in patients whose tumors have resistant EGFR mutations.

description.text: Updated Pediatric Use (8.4) labeling with results from pediatric study 1200.120 fulfilling the Written Request

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for updates to the Use in Specific Populations, Pediatric Use (8.4) subsection of the package insert (PI) to include the results from clinical study 1200.120, conducted to fulfill the April 7, 2017, original Written Request for pediatric studies for afatinib, as amended by our August 14, 2017, June 5, 2019, April 29, 2020 and July 26, 2021, amended Written Request Letters. Additional revisions were made to the Patient Package Insert to better align with FDA regulations, labeling guidelines, policies and practices.

summary.text: Gilotrif (afatinib) received a standard full (non-accelerated) approval under priority review for first-line EGFR mutation-positive metastatic NSCLC, based on a statistically significant PFS improvement in the pivotal Study 1200.32 (LUX-Lung 3), with concurrent approval of the therascreen EGFR companion diagnostic; the product carried an orphan drug designation for this indication, and no advisory committee was convened.

citations.quote: A statistically significant improvement in PFS as determined by the IRC was demonstrated for patients randomized to GILOTRIF compared with those randomized to chemotherapy. See Table 3 and Figure 1. There was no statistically significant difference for overall survival between the treatment arms at the interim analysis conducted at 84% of the planned events for the final analysis.
Because this drug product for this indication has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.

Tumor samples from 264 patients (178 randomized to afatinib and 86 patients randomized to chemotherapy) were tested retrospectively by the companion diagnostic *therascreen® EGFR RGQ PCR Kit, which will be approved concurrent with the approval of afatinib.
